findings.description: This bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects are stored with only SSE-S3 defaults at best; sensitive reports are not protected with a customer-managed KMS key, and encryption is not enforced via a bucket policy that denies unencrypted PUTs.

No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or aws_s3_bucket_acl is defined for this bucket, leaving it without explicit public-access safeguards or an explicit private ACL, so account-level defaults determine exposure rather than the configuration.
The ledger export bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so financial ledger exports are stored without enforced encryption using a customer-managed key.

No public access block is configured for the ledger bucket; an ACL of "private" alone does not prevent a later bucket-policy change from exposing the data, and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource protects it.
The model artifacts bucket has versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, so ML model artefacts are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is defined for this bucket, so its exposure depends on account-level defaults rather than being explicitly restricted.
The runbooks bucket stores operational documentation without any server_side_encryption_configuration, so contents are not encrypted with a customer-managed key.
No public access block is configured for the runbooks bucket, leaving its public exposure to be governed by account-level settings rather than explicit configuration.

The audit trail bucket is the primary log sink and defines no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block; tampering with or exposing audit logs undermines the audit trail, and "log-delivery-write" grants write access to the log delivery group by design.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The audit_trail bucket that receives model_artifacts logs has no logging configuration of its own and no separate destination, so access to the audit log store itself is unaudited.

The seed object sources resources/vendor-roster.xlsx from the repository and uploads it to S3, embedding sensitive vendor data (including third-party personal/business information) directly in version control; repository contents must be treated as compromised.
